title: What You Ask of a Friend
summary: Fourteenth night. Ulli is in the empty Cradle with his back to the wall, singing the fallow song. Jonah asks: carry me on the nineteenth, say I went in. He names the cost he cannot count: when the College reads the road, Ulli is read as having lied. Ulli: you have counted it like a slate; I am not on the slate, I am the one who carries. Why he is alive: nine years in the Deep, because when the wall reached for him in the first month he sang, the way Marl sings to a field, and the wall went still, listening, and has never finished. He was made the one who carries because he was the only man it would not take; forty-three, each sung slow. His price: on the eighteenth he will sit down in the Cradle and stop singing and go, on purpose, the day he has been choosing for nine years, so that two gone in a week is a story and not a question; and Jonah will sit with him and sing. 'You give the bowl back. I'm asking you, once, to take one.' Jonah takes it. His name: Ullan of Marl, the east fields, two l's; they always get it wrong; there was a thing he did on Marl that is his and he keeps it, and Jonah will write that too. On the road Jonah asks Tacitus, for the first time, a thing not for himself: to stand between when the wall takes Ullan, so he can be there and not have the count go through him. It does the deciding thing and then something smaller, in the middle of him: a hand on the arm. Pell: two l's; the east fields flood in spring; he will sing the fallow song with him; three is what a Marl field gets at the end.

events.description: Jonah finds Ulli in the empty Cradle singing the fallow song, and asks him to carry him on the nineteenth and say he went in; he names the cost he cannot count.

Why Ulli is alive nine years in a two-year Deep: he sang when the wall reached for him and it went still, listening, and never finished; he was made the one who carries because it would not take him; forty-three sung slow.

Ulli's price: on the eighteenth he will sit in the Cradle and stop singing and go on purpose, the day he has chosen for nine years, so two gone in a week is a story not a question; Jonah will sit with him and sing. 'I'm asking you, once, to take one.' Jonah takes it.
His name: Ullan of Marl, the east fields, two l's; the Throat wrote it with one; a thing he did on Marl that is his and he keeps; Jonah will write that there was a thing and it was his.

On the road Jonah asks Tacitus, for the first time, a thing not for himself: to stand between when the wall takes Ullan. It does the deciding thing and then something smaller in the middle of him: a hand on the arm, with no hand.

Pell: 'Ullan's in the Cradle. He's not carrying anybody.' Two l's; the east fields flood in spring; the fallow song tells the water the crop is in; he will sing it with him; three is what a Marl field gets at the end.

opening_hook: On the fourteenth night Ulli was not on his bucket, and Jonah found him in the Cradle, singing to it.
closing_hook: Three is what a Marl field gets at the end, and the road will call it the Deep, and be right.
notes: Ulli's full name Ullan of Marl. He will go in on the eighteenth; Jonah sits with him (ch.28 opens with it) then Harrow discovers the plan and demands in (ch.28). Grade about 32. Tacitus has answered a request that was not for Jonah.
